newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-AMERICANS BEAT COSTA RICA TO ADVANCE IN WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AMERICANS BEAT COSTA RICA TO ADVANCE IN WORLD CUP.

text.p: The United States beat Costa Rica 2-1 in a bad-tempered World Cup qualifying match Saturday to advance to the final CONCACAF regional round for the 1998 championships in France.

Costa Rica are almost certain to advance if they beat Trinidad next week, but Guatemala's chances are slim, since they would have to beat the Americans in El Salvador next week and hope Costa Rica lose their last match against the unfancied Trinidadians.

Goals from Brian McBride and Roy Lassiter gave the United States victory Saturday and revenge for a bruising loss by the same score two weeks ago in Costa Rica in the CONCACAF group A. Ronald Gomez pulled a goal back for the visitors late in the game in a match that saw seven yellow cards issued.
The Americans were playing without top-scorer Eric Wynalda, who was suspended after receiving his second yellow card warning two weeks ago.

Already through to the final six-team group from which three countries will go to the World Cup finals in France from the Central and North American and Caribbean region are Mexico, Jamaica, Canada and El Salvador.

A glorious pass from the centre circle to the right wing by Claudio Reyna set up the Americans' first-half goal. Ernie Stewart put across a first-time centre and the Costa Rican defence had difficulty clearing and the ball fell to McBride, whose low right-foot shot from 10 metres beat goalkeeper Hermidio Barrantos.

In the 60th minute, Lassiter who was the leading goalscorer in Major League Soccer's inaugural season, scored the second U.S. goal, hooking in from close range after Alexi Lalas's low shot was fumbled into the air by Barrantos.
Gomez nodded in a cross from Wilmer Lopez in the 75th minute but the U.S. defence held out.

The acrimonious match also saw an unusual incident when Mexican referee Francisco Borja first showed a red card in the 35th minute to U.S. goalkeeper Brad Friedel for stepping outside the penalty area with the ball after a dangerous challenge by Costa Rica's Paulo Wanchope.

The U.S. players besieged the referee and after several minutes and a conference with the linesman, the referee inexplicably withdrew the red card and instead gave Friedel a yellow and awarded the Costa Ricans a free kick.
There appeared to be a lot of bad blood between the teams, who played two weeks ago in Costa Rica in a game in which the Americans were pelted with all kinds of objects in losing 2-1.

United States: Brad Friedel, Alexi Lalas, Jeff Agoos, Eddie Pope, Mike Burns, Cobi Jones (Jovan Kirovski, 84th minute), Claudio Reyna (Joe-Max Moore 81st), John Harkes, Ernie Stewart, Brian McBride, Roy Lassiter

Costa Rica: Hermidio Barrantos, Luis Marin, Ronald Gonzalez, Javier Delgado, Mauricio Solis, Wilmer Lopez, Oscar Ramirez, Jaffet Soto (Roy Myers, 64th), Hernan Medford (Allan Oviedo, 64th), Ronald Gomez, Paulo Wanchope
